page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical AMD EPYC cores on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and is bundled with 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance across memory and processing tasks. The server achieves top-tier status in large-block memory write bandwidth and single-threaded data compression, alongside strong results in large-block read bandwidth and overall Passmark memory scores. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via Geekbench and stress-ng, consistently ranks in the top 25%, supported by hardware-level instruction sets such as AVX-512 and SHA extensions. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also demonstrate strong capabilities, processing 63.9 million operations per second.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of a fast, large-capacity local NVMe SSD, this server offers a resource-dense profile suitable for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It is well-suited for hosting relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance without the noisy-neighbor issues common in shared-core environments.
